_comment: How the people in a town behave when nobody is watching. Drives rise on their own and are spent by doing the thing that answers them, which is what makes a townsperson walk somewhere for a reason rather than jitter around a home point. Openers and replies are the offline fallback: with a model configured, personas.py writes the exchange instead and these stand until it lands. Keep every line under ~120 characters -- two of them share one dialogue panel.

worship.did: stood a while in the shrine.

openers: There was a hare in the low field burning gold. Gold. A hare.
That is the third marked beast this month, and nobody counts them but me.
They say she started with a moth. One moth, and look at us.
replies: My grandmother would have put it out of its misery. I could not.
It cannot stop running. That is the part I cannot get past.
Somebody fixed that light in there. It did not climb in by itself.

openers: Two more houses went dark on the north row. Nobody has been through them.
The lamps were lit the whole way to the bridge when I was small.
It is not that the light goes. It is that nobody comes to look at it.
replies: A reader would fix it. We have not had a reader in years.
I keep mine lit. That is one house out of forty.
You say that every year and every year there are fewer.

openers: The Warden turned another one away today. Attacked every turn, apparently.
You cannot get past the crossing without a seal. I have watched them try.
They say the fourth one has been down. Underneath, I mean.
replies: Good. Half of them would get an animal killed inside a week.
A seal is a promise you can be trusted with something alive.
Down where? -- Do not answer that. I do not want it in my head.

openers: That one with the hound. Came out of the grass with nothing on her.
A probe, they said. Sent to find where the light is going.
She takes the labels *off*. I have seen her do it.
replies: Then she is either the best thing to happen here or the last.
The hound is the strange part. Nobody ever marked that line.
Off, and the animal walks away. I did not know it could come off.

openers: Cold coming off the water. Early for it.
The beds want turning before the rain.
Quiet week. I have sold four things and three were bread.
replies: It always is, this side of the bridge.
I will lend you the fork if you bring it back this time.
Quiet is not the worst thing a week can be.
